How to read this chart

  • ₹2,000 or less has zero MDR, so a ₹2,000 payment is settled in full.
  • Above ₹2,000, MDR is 0.4% of the payment, and 18% GST is added on top of the MDR.
  • MDR stops rising at ₹300, reached at ₹75,000. Every payment above that has the same ₹354 total deduction.
  • The customer always pays the same amount; the deduction comes out of the merchant's settlement.

When this chart does not apply

  • Small merchants whose UPI QR receipts are under ₹1 lakh a month pay zero MDR.
  • Concessional sectors (railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, utility bills, educational institutions) pay a flat ₹5 instead of 0.4%.
  • Mutual funds and stock brokers pay 0.02%, max ₹300.
  • RuPay credit card payments on UPI follow card MDR rates instead.
  • Person-to-person transfers never attract MDR.

For these cases, or any other amount, use the UPI MDR calculator. The full rules are explained in UPI charges above ₹2,000: new rules.

Quick answers

How much MDR is charged on a ₹5,000 UPI payment?

₹20 MDR plus ₹3.60 GST, a total of ₹23.60. The merchant receives ₹4,976.40.

How much MDR is charged on a ₹10,000 UPI payment?

₹40 MDR plus ₹7.20 GST, a total of ₹47.20. The merchant receives ₹9,952.80.

How much MDR is charged on a ₹50,000 UPI payment?

₹200 MDR plus ₹36 GST, a total of ₹236. The merchant receives ₹49,764.

How much MDR is charged on a ₹1 lakh UPI payment?

MDR is capped at ₹300, plus ₹54 GST, a total of ₹354. The merchant receives ₹99,646.
